blocks.text: The Dutch value directness (direct zijn, zeggen waar het op staat): they give their opinion openly, also to their boss, and see this as honesty, not rudeness. British speakers, used to understatement, can find this blunt; the Dutch, in turn, often miss the criticism hidden in British politeness.

blocks.title: Doe maar gewoon, dan doe je al gek genoeg
blocks.text: This saying (just act normal, that's crazy enough) sums up a Dutch attitude: don't show off, don't be pretentious. Bragging about money or status is frowned upon. Modesty and plain speaking are valued.

At a Dutch birthday party (verjaardag) guests often sit in a circle (de kring). You congratulate not only the birthday person but also their family: Gefeliciteerd met je moeder! (Congratulations on your mother's birthday!) Everything is planned: friends make appointments weeks ahead, and de agenda rules social life.

blocks.title: Coalitions and polder
blocks.text: No Dutch party ever has a majority, so governments are always coalitions, formed after long negotiations (de formatie). The Dutch habit of reaching compromise through talking is called the poldermodel: overleggen (consulting) until everyone can live with the result.
Fill in the missing word. The answers are on the last page.

items.q: Ik kijk even in mijn ______ of ik tijd heb.
items.full: Ik kijk even in mijn agenda of ik tijd heb.

items.q: Zullen we ______ betalen? Iedereen betaalt voor zichzelf.
items.full: Zullen we Nederlands betalen? Iedereen betaalt voor zichzelf.

items.q: Doe maar ______, dan doe je al gek genoeg.
items.full: Doe maar gewoon, dan doe je al gek genoeg.

items.q: De ______ Kamer stemt volgende week over de nieuwe wet.
items.full: De Tweede Kamer stemt volgende week over de nieuwe wet.
Na de verkiezingen begint de formatie.
Drie partijen vormen samen een coalitie.
